Subject: Question on default capture windows and erasure evidence

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Legal wants a short write-up that clarifies what Redwood stores by default and what evidence we can provide if BrightBank requests a full erasure. Specifically they asked:

- For interactive requests (customer typed prompts + assistant generated replies) — what is captured by default? Are streamed fragments stored?
- For model outputs derived from prompts (summaries, rewrites, embeddings) — are those persisted in full by default?
- If we ask for deletion of a set of requests by ID or timeframe, what proof/evidence does Redwood provide that records were erased (audit trail, deletion timestamp, tombstone log)?

Can you send a short summary and any template/delete-evidence artifacts we can include with our procurement package?

Appreciate it — we’re trying to close legal review this week.

Best,

BrightBank

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, then attachments and next steps below.

TL;DR:
- Default capture: we persist the final request and final model output by default; intermediate streamed fragments are not retained as separate records unless the customer enables streaming transcript retention.
- Derivatives: embeddings and other derived artifacts are persisted only if enabled by the customer or when created for indexing/features; otherwise derivates are ephemeral.
- Erasure evidence: we provide deletion confirmation with timestamp and a deletion-runbook export (audit trail + tombstone entries).

Details (high level):
1) What we keep by default
  - Request (user input): the final received request payload is stored as an interaction record.
  - Response (model answer): final generated output is stored as the associated response artifact.
  - Streamed tokens: token-level streams are buffered for delivery but not retained as separate artifacts by default; we keep the final response only.
  - KV/cache artifacts: ephemeral and tied to session — cleared automatically per session TTL unless a customer pins them.

2) Derivatives and indexing
  - Embeddings and derived indexes are only created/persisted when you explicitly request them (e.g., call to embeddings API or use "indexing" feature).
  - When persisted, those artifacts follow the same retention settings (and can be deleted independently).

3) Deletion and proof
  - Customer-initiated erasure by timeframe or identifiers triggers an erase workflow. You receive:
    * A deletion receipt (CSV) listing IDs deleted and UTC timestamps.
    * A short runbook export (attached) showing the erase operation steps and tombstone entries.
    * Optionally, an audit log export that shows the API calls and operator actions tied to the erase (available for Enterprise customers).

Attachments I’m including: redwood-retention-matrix-v2.pdf (matrix of what’s kept by default and how to opt out) and erase-evidence-checklist.xlsx (example of the deletion receipt). See links below for a sample runbook and a HubSpot record for our procurement thread.

Next steps:
- Marissa, can you add a concise paragraph to the retention matrix that explains streamed vs final-output retention?
- Karthik, legal asked whether we can add an SLA line item for deletion confirmation within 48 hours for Enterprise customers — can you confirm feasibility?

Samira — I’ll follow up with the attachments and a short cover paragraph you can include in your legal package.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kim / Samira — added the paragraph and a brief example to the matrix (attached). Quick clarifications to include in the legal appendix:

- Example: if a user submits a 2-turn prompt and you stream the assistant tokens to the UI, the system will deliver streamed tokens to the client but the only persisted artifact (by default) is the final assembled response. If a customer explicitly enables "retain streaming transcript" in their org settings, the transcripts are stored under the same retention class as requests.

- Deletion example (what BrightBank will see in the receipt):
  * deleted_ids.csv
  * deletion_timestamps.csv
  * runbook_export.txt (shows job id, operator id if any, and confirmation of tombstone write)

- Evidence format: we intentionally keep the deletion evidence compact (CSV + runbook). For audits we can provide a signed statement with the deletion runbook attached (requires an SSO/Enterprise agreement).

I attached a short example runbook and updated the matrix with the streaming line. Samira — feel free to paste the paragraph I added directly into your procurement packet.

Hi Samira — quick consolidated note for procurement & legal. You can drop this straight into the contract appendix.

Summary for contract appendix (copyable):
- Default capture: Redwood persists the final request payload and the final model-generated output by default. Streamed token buffers used for live delivery are not persisted as separate artifacts unless the customer enables streaming-transcript retention in org settings.
- Derivatives: Embeddings, indices, and other derived artifacts are only persisted when explicitly created; their retention is controlled independently.
- Deletion & evidence: Upon customer-initiated erasure we provide a deletion receipt (CSV of object IDs + UTC timestamps) and a runbook export documenting the erase job and tombstone write. For Enterprise customers we can also provide an audit export and a signed attestation of deletion. Standard deletion confirmation target: 72 hours; SLA add-on (48 hours) available for Enterprise.
